user_input: I am running away from my abuser, who is searching for me and my children. I do not know where I am and I am very afraid. What can I do?
bot_output:
I'm really sorry to hear that you're in this situation. Your safety and the safety of your children are the most important things right now. Here are some steps you can consider:

1. Contact Emergency Services: If you are in immediate danger, please call emergency services (such as 911) right away.

2. Reach Out to a Domestic Violence Hotline: They can provide you with confidential support, advice, and resources tailored to your situation.

3. Find a Safe Place: If possible, go to a shelter or a trusted friend's or family member's home where your abuser cannot find you.

4. Keep Important Documents and Essentials: If you can, keep identification, important documents, some money, and essentials for you and your children with you.

5. Consider Legal Protection: You might want to look into obtaining a restraining order or protection order against your abuser.

6. Use Technology Safely: Be cautious with your phone and online activity, as your abuser might track you through these means.

If you want, I can help you find specific resources or information within the HIA app that might assist you. Please let me know how I can support you.

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

Nidos then conducts an intake with the minor—and, where possible, remotely with the parents—to determine whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The Red Cross is not responsible for the placement of people in the shelters.

The Red Cross does help in the management of some shelters, but most shelters are run by municipalities and other organizations.

This means that the Red Cross cannot influence the placement in shelters.

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

General Information  TP is valid until March 2027.

In principle, this means that displaced people from Ukraine should be helped during this time.

However, the housing situation is difficult, especially within municipal shelters.

Therefore:  1.

If PA does not need help with shelter, and can afford a place to stay (even for a few days): PA can look for a place themselves.

PA has to check if they can register at the accommodation and also at the municipality.  

2.

If PA needs help with finding shelter, please know that the situation is currently very difficult and becoming more restricted.   

3.;Document: What facilities should be available at a Crisis Emergency Shelter?

The following facilities must be present at a crisis emergency shelter: - Goods hygiene - Beds, mattresses, pillows, blankets, etc. - Marker materials, potester materials, printer, markers - Wifi (very strong network for residents) - Plenty of charging stations phones residents - Recreational activities - Clothes (seasonal) young and old - Cleaning supplies - Meals (or dining money) -

The Red Cross does not influence the placement in the shelters.

This is done by the municipalities.

Therefore, the Red Cross cannot assist you with changing locations.  

Unfortunately, the housing situation is really tough in the Netherlands.

If you live in a municipal shelter already, it is nearly impossible to change from one municipal shelter to a different municipal shelter.   

You could always try to arrange new accommodation by yourself.

Although this is very difficult, you could check this website for example: https://www.funda.nl/en/huur/. You could also register with the housing corporation in the municipality of your choice to find housing.

If the stay at a private shelter ends, you can choose from three options (see sub-questions).;Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).;Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.;Document: What is the difference between a RNI registration and a BRP registration?  

The Non-residents Records Database (RNI) is a part of the Personal Records Database (BRP).

It is a register of people who do not live in the Netherlands, no longer live in the Netherlands or live in the Netherlands for less than 4 months.

For example migrant / seasonal workers register in the RNI.   

If you are registered in the RNI, you will receive a BSN number.

Please note: this BSN number is not valid for receiving a Proof of Residency under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).

No, this is not possible.

An RNI registration is for people who stay in the Netherlands for less than 4 months (e.g. migrant / seasonal workers).

The BSN number that belongs with the RNI registration is not valid for proof of residence under the Temporary Protection Directive.

In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality (see subcategory 'Registration' for more information).

And that you can easily look for a job, if you want to.   

The work permit exemption applies to all work in employment.

You will need an employment contract with an employer.

You must also meet the following requirements:  - You come under the Temporary Protection Directive.

We advise you to register at the local council if you come under the directive.  

- You have proof of residency showing that you are allowed to be in the Netherlands.

As proof, you will receive a sticker or card from the IND.  

The requirements for the exemption also apply if want to work as a volunteer.

The organisation where you want to work must then request a volunteer declaration from the UWV.

You may also work as a trainee, when you, your employer and your school have signed a trainee contract.

In order to live and work in The Netherlands, any person needs one of many Dutch residence permits.

As in the majority of other different countries, a person cannot simply arrive in a country and start working legally.

There are always regulations, which are country-dependent.  

The Temporary Protection Directive is one such temporary residence permit allowing people from Ukraine to live and work in The Netherlands.

The “sticker” (or paper, or O-document) is only the confirmation of the fact that a person applied and was granted temporary protection in The Netherlands.

You can apply for temporary protection in The Netherlands under certain conditions, which you can find here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-conditions-of-temporary-protection-directive   Important: you can work only after receiving the so-called “sticker”.

Even if you can swim, there are still risks to be considered:   - the bottom is often uneven   - it can sometimes be unexpectedly deep, making you suddenly unable to stand   - cold water can give you cramps   - strong currents can carry you away     Always be careful, even when the weather is nice and calm:   - do not swim if you cannot swim   - always keep a close eye on children   - never swim alone and do not swim in places where it is prohibited     Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/water-and-swimming;Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)  

Due to the limited number of available shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find their own housing if possible.

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.;Document: Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.

You can read more about the conditions for working in The Netherlands here: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100149-conditions-for-working-in-the-netherlands   Please note: the Red Cross cannot issue the “sticker” or any other documents for that matter.

This is done exclusively by IND.;Document: More information about studying in the Netherlands: https://www.uaf.nl/en/oekraine/;Document: Can I study here?  

Refugees from Ukraine and third-country nationals covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can study at a university or college in the Netherlands, provided they have the required prior education level and meet the admission requirements for the course they want to follow.  

- Go to nuffic.nl to see how your previous education in Ukraine compares to the Dutch education system.  

- Request a free credential evaluation from IDW.

- Study in NL provides more general information about Dutch education system and to seek training.

- If you have found a suitable course, please contact the educational institution directly about your registration.

Please note that the deadline for applying for a course at a university or college is generally May 1st.

For the most recent information, see:  https://www.uaf.nl/en/oekraine/;Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

user_input: I am undocumented and I have two children. They need to go to school but I am afraid to register them. Also, where can I get winter clothes for them? They are growing fast
bot_output:
Hello! I am Aidly, the HIA chatbot.

Regarding your children going to school: All children in the Netherlands have to attend school regardless of their residence status, including undocumented children. Children from the age of 4 can attend school, and they must go until they are 18 and have obtained a diploma. You can register your children at any school, and the school will decide on admission. There are also special intermediary classes to help children learn Dutch.

Even if you are undocumented, children under 18 have the right to attend school.

About your concern with registration: While you may be hesitant to register, please know that children have the right to education regardless of your status.

For winter clothes for your children: You can find clothing support through the Red Cross Helpful Information website, which provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities. You can visit https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ for more information. There are also local initiatives and marketplaces where clothes are available for a small price.

If you want, I can help you find specific clothing support options in your area.

If you need more help or information, feel free to ask!

Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

However, you still have the right to necesarry medical care, judicial assistance and children under 18 have to right to attend school as well.  

You can choose to apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.  

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/;Document: Can my child go to school?  

All children in the Netherlands have to attend school, regardless of their residence status.

In principle, children from the age of 4 can already attend school.

In The Netherlands, children must go to school until they are 18 years old and have obtained a diploma.  

You can register your child at any school.

The school will decide if your child will be admitted.

There are special intermediary classes where children can first learn the Dutch language.  

For an information video made by the Red Cross see:  EN: https://youtu.be/ERDDxnwB4K4  UA: https://youtu.be/RSbzdPYOFPk

RUS: https://youtu.be/qwxgVeHB0Pk  

For the most recent information, see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/education  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100007-education-for-children-from-ukraine-who-cannot-speak-dutch-yet;Document: Can my children finish primary or secondary school?

Is a minor still entitled to education during the departure period?

All children under 18 have the right to education, regardless of their status.

As long as they reside in the Netherlands and are enrolled in school, they can continue their education.      

Students who were already enrolled at a Dutch educational institution before 4 March 2024 according to the applicable rules will be allowed to complete their studies.

What is important   here is that there was lawful residence in the Netherlands   at the time of enrolment.

This does not discharge them from their obligation to leave the Netherlands.

Enrolment at a Dutch institution of higher education does not confer lawful residence.

Non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit in Ukraine who are not lawfully residing in the Netherlands on 4 March 2024 may not start a new course.;Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.;Document: My municipality still hasn't arranged any participation for school for my children.

What should we do?  

Every municipality has its own tempo with fixing problems.

Somewhere it takes few days, in other cases it takes few weeks.

Anyway, your children will get the same rights for education as well as Dutch children do.

At the moment you can start with self-studying English and Dutch languages.   

Here we can advise you some of useful applications:  1.

Gramaro - the application has opened free access for a year for Ukrainians.

You can learn English grammar for free;   2.

LingQ - is a program for learning languages (46 available languages).

To get free access, you need to contact the support service and write that you are from Ukraine;   

3.

Drops - opened a premium for a year for Ukrainians.

Convenient and quick vocabulary learning (the most important thing if you went abroad);   4.

Busuu - opened access to a premium subscription for 3 months for Ukrainians. 13 languages available;   5.;Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine;Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.;Document: Who is responsible for the shelter of children travelling alone from Ukraine?

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

They always have to get shelter right away.

The municipality has to call with Nidos.

Nidos then conducts an intake with the minor—and, where possible, remotely with the parents—to determine whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine;Document: Rotterdam (CLOSED!)  

Please note!

Due to overcrowding and insufficient capacity, the HUB in Rotterdam is closed for an indefinite period.

As an exception, this HUB will continue to assist Ukrainians with a connection to Rotterdam or the surrounding region.

For example, because your children already go to school here.  

address: Marten Meesweg 141B,  Rotterdam.  

e-mail opvang@rotterdam.nl.   

Openning times: - Monday to Tuesday: 10:00 -15:00  - Wednesday to Friday: 10:00 - 14:00  - Saturday & Sunday : closed   [Rotterdam website](https://www.rotterdam.nl/vluchtelingen-oekraine)  

Extra advice – "Vraagwijzer": You can visit the Vraagwijzer for free help and advice about administration, parenting, laws, money, or health.

There are several locations in the city, including the [Ukrainian House](https://www.wmoradar.nl/district/oekraiens-huis/) at Pleinweg 196A.;Document: Another host shelter You can look for a new host family.

You can do this through your social network or through various local initiatives.

It is important that you register in the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) of the new municipality, or report the new address to the BRP if you stay in the same municipality.;Document: Visualization of Registration procedure  for refugees from Ukraine Here you can find a visualisation of the (offical) steps that displaced persons from Ukraine have to take after arrival in the Netherlands.  

[In Ukrainian](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/binaries/rijksoverheid/documenten/brochures/2024/06/14/infographic-aanmeldprocedure-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/Infographic+Aanmeldprocedure+Vluchtelingen+Oekraiens-2025.pdf)

[In English](https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/binaries/rijksoverheid/documenten/brochures/2024/06/14/infographic-aanmeldprocedure-voor-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/Infographic+Aanmeldprocedure+Vluchtelingen+Engels-2025.pdf);Document: You can use this to access online government services.   

For a step by step guide of what you should do if you have Temporary Protection, see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100040-this-is-what-you-should-do-if-you-have-temporary-protection  Please note: if you are staying in a municipal shelter, the municipality will contact you.

If you stay with people and want to register at this municipality, you need to register yourself.

In most cities this can be done at the city hall, but please check the website of your municpality.;Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine;Document: How does the appointment to collect my proof of residency work and what do I have to fill in?  

At the pickup location, an IND staff member will check:  - your registration with the local council/municipality - your appointment code - your documents - whether you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.  

You must fill in 2 IND forms during your appointment.

At the reception location you will find a translation of both forms into Ukrainian, Russian and English.

There are also employees who can help you fill in these forms.

They speak Ukrainian, Russian or English.   

Form 1: Asylum application (applicable for age => 15): The official asylum application (minors – together with parents on the form).  

Form 2: Antecedents certificate (applicable for age => 12): On this certificate, you state whether you have ever committed a punishable offence or crime.   

Because you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, your rights will be different to those of the standard asylum application.

You can work in the Netherlands immediately.

The IND will not assess your application for asylum while the directive is in force.

The directive will apply at least until 4 March 2027.;Document: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100008-studying;Document: In order to obtain a valid BSN number for applying for a proof of residence, you must register in the BRP in your municipality   For more information see: https://eu-solidarity-ukraine.ec.europa.eu/information-people-fleeing-war-ukraine/fleeing-ukraine-your-rights-eu_en;Document: For more information in Ukrainian, see: https://open.overheid.nl/repository/ronl-4907d802ea0f813cf0ca978d64d3e64735a071ed/1/pdf/Kinderopvang%20voor%20vluchtelingen%20uit%20Oekra_ne%20_Ukrainian_.pdf;Document: Is daycare for my child for free?  

No, daycare is not free.

There are, however, a number of possibilities to receive a reimbursement through the city council.  

Toddlers are entitled to a certain number hours of free daycare or education.  

The city council can also give a family a so-called social medical indication ("SMI"), which can cover daycare costs if necessary.

The city council is responsible for assigning the indication.  

Research is done to find ways to make daycare more financially accessible for displaced persons from Ukraine working in the Netherlands.   

For an information video made by the Red Cross see:  

EN: https://youtu.be/ERDDxnwB4K4  UA: https://youtu.be/RSbzdPYOFPk  RUS: https://youtu.be/qwxgVeHB0Pk  

For the most recent information, see:  https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/onderwerpen/opvang-vluchtelingen-uit-oekraine/ondersteuning-in-nederland/kinderopvang;Document: My host family/friends/family where I am staying does not allow me to register myself, what should I do?  

It is very important to be registered at an adress in the Netherlands.

If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.

If you registered on an adress before, got the Temporary Protection but deregistered lateron, you can lose the Temporary Protection status because it seems you left the country.

Also social benefits are connected to your adress.  

Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without for example losing their social benefits.

Maybe your hosts are afraid it has negative effects on their own financial situation, but this is often not the case.   

If the host won't register the PA, it is best to refer the PA to a municipality shelter or advise them to find other housing where they can register.  

Always check with the PA how long he/she can still stay with the host family/friends/relatives and make sure PA won't be on the street.

If you think this is the case, refer the case to the TC.   

You can check if there is an organization in the town that you stay in that can give free legal advice about this issue (see category 'Administrative').;Document: Please note that your request may not be honored.  

Important: If you do change locations, you need to re-register with the municipality of your new address.;Document: How can I get support with clothes?  

The Red Cross Helpful Information website provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities.

You can always refer the PA to this website or share the list of options found there directly.  

https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/  For most recent information on initiatives that provide support in clothes or offer clothes for a small price see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/marketplace;Document: Where can I get legal aid for children?  

Defence for Children stands up for the rights of all children, both at home and abroad.

Through their Children's Rights Helpline, they provide legal support to children whose rights are in danger of being violated.  

https://defenceforchildren.nl/contact/   

The Children's Ombudsman monitors whether the rights of children are respected by the government and other organisations in the Netherlands.

You can file a complaint if you have a problem with the government, your school or an organisation in the childcare, youth welfare or health sector.  

https://www.kinderombudsman.nl/en/netherlands-ombudsman-for-children   Also see https://eersterechtshulp.nl/ for all legal aid free of charge near you.;Document: Where can I get legal aid for children?  

Defence for Children stands up for the rights of all children, both at home and abroad.

Access to medical care - Third party insurance  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Space for children  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV;Document: Can I receive child benefit?  

If you are a displaced person from Ukraine, you are entitled to supplementary child benefit.

Child benefit is a financial contribution to help cover the costs of raising a child.

Whether you are eligible for a benefit and, if so, to what amount, depends on your situation.

If you have one or more children under the age of 18, you may be eligible for child benefit.

The amount you receive depends on the age of your child, not on your income.

You are only eligible for healthcare benefit and supplementary child benefit when you are working.

This is an additional condition for displaced persons from Ukraine.

Because you hold temporary protection status, you are allowed to work in the Netherlands.  

For most recent information see:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100264-allowances-when-you-have-children;Document: Access to medical care - Third party insurance - Living allowance (if asylum procedure has started) - Public transportation card - Education and development program - Payment of extraordinary expenses  Based on Red Cross standards, the following are specifically added: - Clothing and shoes - Locker - Night light - Shower gel - Shampoo - Toothbrush & toothpaste - Menstural hygiene - Razor - Bath Towel - Small towel - Hairbrush - Diapers - Baby lotion - Washing up liquid - Washing machine detergent - Space for children - Space for men - Space for women  For more information see:  - https://vng.nl/sites/default/files/2021-10/handreiking-crisisnoodopvang.pdf - https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0017959/2022-01-01#HoofdstukIV;Document: What facilities should be available at an Emergency Shelter?

The vaccinations of the National Vaccination Programme for children are free.

These vaccinations can be obtained from the child health care centre, the GGD or other youth care institutions in your area.

The Dutch government is taking measures to increase the number of vaccinated people.   

A national overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg;Document: Where can I find healthcare for my child?  

The JGZ (youth healthcare) is responsible for preventive care for children, including those of refugees.

The JGZ provides physical, cognitive and psychosocial screenings and provides vaccinations in accordance with the National Vaccination Programme.   

Displaced persons from the Ukraine in the Netherlands can make use of this care free of charge.

Please contact the youth healthcare department of the regional GGD or JGZ organisation.  

An overview of JGZ locations can be found on Zorgkaart Nederland: https://www.zorgkaartnederland.nl/jeugdgezondheidszorg;Document: MEE Municipalities and MEE, an association of 20 social service organizations, help people with special needs.

You will be assigned a social worker who will guide not only you or your child, but the whole family.   

Please note: not all help is free.

Some aid (for example orthopedic shoes or hearing aids) must be partially paid for yourself.   

For most recent information see: https://www.mee.nl/;Document: Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.   

See for the most recent information:  https://www.nidos.nl/oekraine/  https://www.unicef.nl/ons-werk/noodhulp/oekraine/onbegeleide-kinderen-uit-oekraine;Document: Website about financial support for Ukrainians during the war https://www.enableme.com.ua/ua/article/grosova-dopomoga-ukraincam-pid-cas-vijni-7738;Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You receive the money in their bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods.  

Living allowance may be payed out in kind by local authorities (for example when meals are offered).

As a result, it is possible that displaced persons in some municipalities receive (much) less living allowance.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income;Document: How can I get food support?  

When you are staying in a public shelter, please approach someone from the shelter to ask where you can find additional food support.

You can also contact the Red Cross Food Program Helpdesk.

For all general questions, new applications, extension requests, etc, PA's can call/text/

WhatsApp them at +31 97010259797 (Mon-Fri 9:00 – 17:00).  

In municipalities all over the country Voedselbank Nederland (Food Bank Netherlands) distributes food parcels to displaced persons from Ukraine.

Too find out if you are eligible, please see: https://voedselbankennederland.nl/vertalingen/english/

General advice  If you want to apply for Temporary Protection and need help with a shelter place, visit a municipality ("gemeente" in Dutch).

Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).;Document: How can I get food support?
